summary: Make `cart remove --quantity N` actually remove N units by issuing one POST /cart/remove per unit, stopping early when the API reports the line is empty.
reason: POST /cart/remove ignores the `quantity` field in its body and always decrements the line by exactly one unit. The generated command sent {"id":N,"quantity":M} once and reported success, so `--quantity 5` silently removed a single unit and the caller had no way to tell. Verified live on 2026-09-22: a 3-unit line sent {"id":36756,"quantity":3} answered {"quantity":2} (one unit removed), and {"quantity":0} also removed exactly one. POST /cart/add does honour quantity, so only the remove side needs the loop.
validated_outcome: Verified live against siteapi.shopper.com.br on the Compra Unica storefront: adding 3 units then removing with --quantity 3 now empties the line in one command instead of leaving 2 behind; the cart was returned to empty after the test. TestRemainingCartQuantityReadsLineQuantity pins the live response shape (including absent/null/unparseable bodies) and TestRemoveRepeatCount pins the loop arithmetic, so collapsing this back into a single call fails the suite. A --stdin body is still sent verbatim exactly once. `--dry-run` renders the request once and notes on stderr how many times it would be sent, rather than echoing N identical blocks.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: The generator should be able to record that a sniffed mutate endpoint ignores one of its own documented body fields, so the emitted command compensates instead of reporting a silent partial write.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: The spec (and the API's own field name) promise a quantity-aware remove; only live dogfooding shows it is per-unit. Nothing in the generated command could detect the mismatch.
